nodes.label: Keep a Changelog record
nodes.rationale: Keep a Changelog 1.1.0 plus SemVer, with an [Unreleased] section carrying Added/Changed/Fixed/Removed/Security; twenty released versions from 0.1.0 (2026-04-27) to 0.16.0 (2026-08-15). Every minor is potentially breaking because the project is pre-1.0.

nodes.label: [Unreleased] window
nodes.rationale: The open window after v0.16.0, dominated by the DevTools UI rebuild (#482 and its parts) and by the comparison-benchmark and toolchain corrections.

nodes.label: DevTools send-message action (#553)
nodes.rationale: Every other panel reads; this one writes, so it is off until acknowledged in code. Two switches and only one is a security decision: panels.send hides the view, allowMessageSending grants the capability — and while the acknowledgement is unset the actors.send method is never registered, so a client is told there is no such method rather than being refused by a guard it might argue with. One bound is structural rather than checked, which is why it holds: the body is JSON, so it cannot be a PoisonPill.

nodes.label: DevTools resolved-configuration panel (#553)
nodes.rationale: A merged tree answers 'what is this setting now'; the question that brings someone here is 'why is it not what I wrote', which needs the layer as well as the value — so Config.load keeps the layers it merged and a config built any other way reports that it cannot attribute rather than guessing. Secrets are redacted by key rather than by value: a password that happens to look ordinary is still a password.

nodes.label: DevTools event-stream panel (#553)
nodes.rationale: Needs EventStream._observe, checked BEFORE the empty-stream early return — an observer placed after it sees nothing on a system nobody else subscribes to, which is exactly the system a developer opens this panel on. The observer installs only while a panel is subscribed, unlike the span tap, because the bus is always live. Events are capped and the panel says how many were dropped: a tail that silently skips is worse than one that admits it.

nodes.label: DevTools dead-letter panel (#553)
nodes.rationale: An undeliverable message throws nothing and logs nothing by default, and that silence is what makes the failure easy to miss. It polls once a second rather than streaming, so DevTools is not on the delivery path of the very failures it watches. The queue being off is said out loud rather than shown as an empty table: 'nothing is broken' and 'nothing is being recorded' are opposite answers an empty table gives identically.

nodes.label: DevTools UI test suite (#487)
nodes.rationale: Roughly 3,000 lines had no tests, which was the migration's whole point. The most valuable cover TapClientService against a socket the test drives, because every one of those failure modes is silent in production: a broken refcount leaves the system producing frames for a panel nobody is looking at, and a missed sequence gap renders a tree that quietly disagrees with the real one. Coverage was measured before and after — 93.68% to 93.54% — as the issue asked rather than assumed.

nodes.label: DevTools charts on Apache ECharts (#486)
nodes.rationale: The actor tree stays DOM and the percentage bars stay CSS deliberately — a tree needs search, selection and copyable paths, and a chart engine behind three lines of CSS is pure overhead. Where ECharts has no answer the geometry stayed ours. The 150 to 200 KiB budget move is a measurement, not a preference: ECharts costs 165.9 KB gzip with a single chart type registered, so the old estimate could not have been met by any import set.

nodes.label: DevTools UI is Angular throughout (#485)
nodes.rationale: withHashLocation() is mandatory rather than stylistic: UiAssetRoutes.ts serves no SPA fallback, so a non-asset path must 404 rather than return the shell, which is what lets one bundle serve at the root and under DevTools.mount('/devtools'). The connection logic was deliberately NOT rewritten — porting it by hand in the same change would have made a regression indistinguishable from a wiring mistake. One defect it found: a computed that mutates during evaluation leaves the view rendering one update behind for ever.

nodes.label: DevTools UI built by Angular 22 instead of Bun.build (#483)
nodes.rationale: A build-time change only. The adapter wraps the shell rather than each panel on purpose: wrapping panels would have meant Angular owning navigation, and with it a shell port smuggled into the issue that was only supposed to change how the bundle is produced. Chunks are attributed to budgets from the builder's metafile rather than file names, since Angular emits chunk-<hash>.js and panel identity survives only in stats.json.

nodes.label: Example frontend bundles no longer committed (#559)
nodes.rationale: 86 tracked files that CI already rebuilds from source. It also retires a question examples.yml documented at length: four of the six builds are not reproducible (Next mints a fresh build id, Svelte stamps a timestamp), so a rebuild-and-diff staleness gate could never have worked — not committing the output dissolves the problem rather than answering it. static/plain and static/lit stay committed because those files are source, not output.

nodes.label: One integration-compose driver replaces 34 broker scripts (#559)
nodes.rationale: The list of backends lived in four places at once — both scripts, both aggregate chains and the CI matrix — and missing one meant the suite simply never ran, silently. The driver discovers suites from the tree; IntegrationBrokerSuites.test.ts fails when matrix and tree disagree in either direction and pins the compose argument vectors, --exit-code-from runner included, since without it a failing scenario inside the container would leave every broker suite green forever.

nodes.label: Bun toolchain pinned via .bun-version (#1328)
nodes.rationale: CI read bun-version: latest at 13 of 14 setup-bun sites, so Bun 1.4.0 would have switched every workflow silently, the way 1.3.14 once broke the badge scrape (#1194). A future bump is now a one-line reviewed change that triggers the gates it affects; the supported floor is unchanged, and the nightly quarantine criterion counts nights only while the pin is unchanged (#1330).

nodes.label: Published comparison figures from a hundred-round Linux run (#1327)
nodes.rationale: Every absolute number moved by a factor of two to five, so the columns are comparable with each other and with nothing quoted before. Three published claims did not survive the move and the pages carry them as corrections rather than restating them quietly — the alternating volley is no longer a tie, and the round-trip row no longer splits by runtime.

nodes.label: Comparison benchmarks run on Linux (#1325)
nodes.rationale: Committed POSIX launchers were recorded at mode 100644, so /bin/sh refused to exec them and every JVM arm died at exit 126. Windows never saw it and no gate did either, because nothing in the repository looked at a file mode; the modes are now asserted against the git INDEX, since the working tree cannot answer that question on Windows — a filesystem check would have passed on the one platform where the bug does not bite. A missing toolchain is now reported as skipped, because a partial run reported as a plain green tick is how a release publishes figures for arms that never ran.

nodes.label: One-way batch read and the merge-before-exit fix (#1326)
nodes.rationale: A one-way call completes when the message is dispatched, not when the grain has processed it, so the read could overtake the tail of the batch; the read is now a bounded drain that still times out on dropped messages, so it remains a completion check rather than a way of passing one. Separately, the driver called process.exit(1) before merging, so one arm failing at round 44 discarded eight other arms' hundred rounds.

nodes.label: formatCount host-dependent grouping fix (#553)
nodes.rationale: Grouping by rewriting the comma out of toLocaleString('en-US') depends on the runtime's ICU data — a comma under Bun, a thin space U+2009 under the Node that runs the UI test suite, where the rewrite therefore hit nothing. Grouped by hand now and pinned by a test that asserts the codepoint rather than the shape.

nodes.label: Voice sample narrowing and a lifted tsconfig exclude (#1015)
nodes.rationale: Array.prototype.find over a union hands back the whole union, and the casts that reached past it are precisely what stopped the mismatch from being visible where it was written. The tsconfig.dev.json exclusion did not match that file's own stated exclude rule — a file is excluded when a manifest other than the root resolves its imports — and drift is not the only thing a typecheck catches. The gate was checked in both directions before the entry was removed.
